claims.evidence: Raw names 2018MMDD_vcs075_<18-1234|18-1310>_Mazzulli_Nandkishore_<S|T><1-4>; each raw is one SILAC mixture (MaxQuant experiment S1..S4/T1..T4 per batch, Multiplicity 2). Paper: neurons sequentially extracted into Triton X-100 soluble and 2% SDS soluble fractions; heavy and light samples of each fraction mixed 1:1; 4 biological replicates (individual culture wells). Each fraction of each genotype culture is a separate measured sample (batch rule 16), so it has its own source name.

claims.location: comment[label], characteristics[cell line], characteristics[genotype], factor value[genotype] rows 1-32
claims.value: SILAC heavy = A53T line (WIBR-iPS-SNCA-A53T); SILAC light = isogenic corrected line (WIBR-iPS-SNCA-A53T-Corr), in all 16 mixtures
claims.evidence: Paper Methods: "The differential protein expression between heavy and light labeled samples were analyzed and expressed as log fold change of heavy over light"; results are reported as A53T relative to corrected (Fig 1B legend: "protein levels obtained from SILAC labeled A53T iPSn relative to corrected lines (dashed line)"). The same lab labelled the treated arm heavy and the vehicle light in the leupeptin/L-DOPA experiment. Data check (orientation.txt): NONO and SFPQ log2 H/L +1.57..+2.13 (batch 18-1234) and +0.50..+1.16 (18-1310) in every SDS run and negative in every Triton run, PSPC1/FUS likewise positive in SDS: matches the paper's insoluble NONO/SFPQ/FUS/PSPC1 increase in A53T (Fig 1A, 2A). CYFIP2, CADPS, PRKAR2A, MAPT log2 H/L negative in all Triton runs of both batches: matches the reported decrease of CYFIP2/CADPS (Fig 4E, SILAC-MS) and PRKAR2A (Fig 6I) in PD iPSn. No replicate shows the opposite sign -> no label swap. No explicit sentence "heavy = A53T" exists in the accessible text; the map rests on H/L = A53T/Corr reporting plus the data.

claims.location: characteristics[protein solubility fraction], factor value[protein solubility fraction] rows 1-32
claims.value: T runs = Triton X-100 soluble fraction; S runs = Triton X-100 insoluble SDS soluble fraction
claims.evidence: Paper/PRIDE protocol: sequential extraction in 1% Triton X-100 then 2% SDS, both fractions analysed. File letters T/S; corroborated by the data: aggregation-prone NONO/SFPQ ratios rise in S and fall in T, the paper's soluble->insoluble shift. Custom characteristics column (spec "Extending Templates"); a biochemical fraction measured as a sample is a characteristic/factor, not comment[fraction identifier] (batch rule 16).

claims.value: 1-4 = wells 1-4 of batch 18-1234, 5-8 = wells 1-4 of batch 18-1310, numbered within each (genotype, solubility fraction) group
claims.evidence: Paper: "P-values of 4 biological replicates (individual culture wells)"; n=4 culture wells in Fig 1B. Two harvests (day 60 and day 90 per Data availability) are two separately submitted core batches 18-1234 and 18-1310, i.e. different cultures, so numbers are unique per culture within each factor-value group (README.adoc:330, rule 3). S<n> and T<n> of one batch are the two sequential extracts of the same well and share the number.
Core submission ids in the raw names (20180420 ... 18-1234, 20180611 ... 18-1310), searched separately (txt_18_1234.7z / txt_18_1310.7z).

claims.value: A53T rows: autosomal dominant Parkinson disease 1 (MONDO:0008200); Corr rows: normal (PATO:0000461)
claims.evidence: Lines derived from a PD patient heterozygous for SNCA A53T (PARK1/PARK-SNCA; Soldner 2011: patient described in Golbe 1996). The corrected line carries no pathogenic variant and is the study's control; the project-level disease is not broadcast to it (reconcile guidance). MONDO label verified in OLS.

Paper: iPSC-midbrain dopaminergic neuron cultures (differentiated 40 days, neurobasal/SM1 to day 60-90); PRIDE organism part GO:1904948 midbrain dopaminergic neuron differentiation. CL label verified in OLS.

Paper: "The A53T a-syn mutation harboring iPSc and its isogenic line were kindly provided by Dr. Rudolf Jaenisch"; Cuddy 2019 identifies them as the Soldner 2011 lines, whose names are WIBR-iPS-SNCA(A53T) and WIBR-iPS-SNCA(A53T)-Corr. Both derive from one patient, hence one individual. No study patient ID is published; the identifier is constructed from the line name.

limitations: Supplementary tables (NIHMS1994206-supplement-2..14.xlsx, incl. Table S1 d90 solubility and Table S9 A53T vs Corr) could not be retrieved: PMC bin URLs served a reCAPTCHA page (not bypassed), Europe PMC supplementaryFiles returned a connection error, cell.com returned a Cloudflare 403. The channel map therefore rests on the Methods (H/L reported as A53T relative to Corr) plus the deposited ratios, not on an explicit "heavy = A53T" sentence.

Culture age per batch is not documented: the Data availability says the deposit holds day 60 and day 90 data, but which of 18-1234 / 18-1310 is day 60 vs day 90 is not stated. The data hint 18-1234 = day 90 (larger NONO/SFPQ insolubility, which the paper says increases from d60 to d90) but this was not adopted (biological-direction inference); no sampling-time column was written, the batch is recorded in comment[sample preparation batch].

MaxQuant searches also contain experiments F1-F4 per batch (raws ..._F1..F4, MS/MS identification 0.1-2%) that were NOT deposited; they are absent from the SDRF. Their nature is not described in the paper.

Donor age, sex, ancestry and Cellosaurus accession are not available: no Cellosaurus entry for the Soldner WIBR-iPS-SNCA lines; the Khurana re-derived line CVCL_E3C7 (Female 49Y, Caucasian Italian, Contursi kindred) is probably the same donor but this is not stated for these lines, so its values were not copied.

Assumption: the S<n> and T<n> raws of a batch are the sequential Triton and SDS extracts of the same culture well (paper: sequential extraction of each culture); the paper does not state the well numbering explicitly.
The paper says gel lanes were cut into 2-4 bands, but one raw file per sample was deposited; no fractionation column was written and fraction identifier is 1.
comment[precursor mass tolerance] = not available (not recorded by MaxQuant 1.6.0.16 output; no mqpar.xml), so parse_sdrf convert-openms is expected to fail on it.
Digestion protease is not named in the paper or PRIDE record; Trypsin is inferred from the MaxQuant Trypsin/P search rule (reconcile MINOR cleavage_agent_unsupported).
PRIDE metadata errors overridden: instrument LTQ Orbitrap Elite (raw headers say Q Exactive HF); identifiedPTMStrings "No PTMs".
